text:
priya: heads-up — after the recent change to package exports in @sdk we started seeing onboarding sample failures for both Node and edge runtimes. repro in the quickstart: `yarn workspace sample-app start`

alex: ugh, saw that when I ran the worker sample this morning. error is `Error: Cannot find module './dist/node/index.cjs'` in CI.

maria: is this the conditional exports switch to only expose `./dist/edge.mjs` and `./dist/node.mjs`? we used to rely on `main`/`module` fallbacks for samples.

priya: yes — PR #432 changed exports to be stricter. We wanted to avoid accidental consumption of source `src/` in packages, but it broke apps that do `require('sdk')` or do old-style `import sdk from 'sdk'`.

jamal: quick paste of the failing stack from worker logs:
```
TypeError: The requested module 'sdk' does not provide an export named 'default'
    at file:///workspace/sample-app/edge/entry.mjs:3:23
    at ModuleJob.run (internal/modules/esm/module_job.js:152:23)
```

priya: Cloudflare worker sample uses `import sdk from 'sdk'` expecting a default export. Node sample uses `const sdk = require('sdk')`. Both are incompatible with the current exports map.

sam: CI also flagged auth retries failing in integration tests — might be related when the wrong bundle (edge vs node) gets picked and polyfills differ.

maria: can we add a conditional exports map covering both cjs & esm entrypoints? Something like:
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "node": {
      "require": "./dist/node/cjs/index.cjs",
      "import": "./dist/node/esm/index.mjs"
    },
    "default": "./dist/edge/esm/index.mjs"
  }
}
```
This should give Node `require()` a CJS path and edge/ESM an MJS path.

priya: that looks reasonable. two concerns: 1) typings — our `types` field currently points to `types/index.d.ts` but if consumers import subpaths we might need to expose `./*` patterns. 2) bundle size — we want to avoid shipping both CJS + ESM in every install if possible.

jamal: for typings we can add `"exports": { "./*": { "types": "./dist/types/*.d.ts" } }` — but npm export patterns don't allow globs. maybe publish top-level `types` and keep declaration files in `dist/types` and reference via `types` main pointer.

alex: quick hack for onboarding samples: update sample imports to explicit subpath `import sdk from 'sdk/edge'` or `const sdk = require('sdk/node')` — but that's not great for new users.

priya: agreed — onboarding should be copy-paste friendly. I'd prefer package to keep parity: default import works for both edge & node with graceful resolution.

ci-bot: build failed — samples/sample-app/edge: missing export 'default' (see https://ci.internal/redwood-inference/sdk/432)

sam: proposal: revert the strict exports change on `main` branch, then open a follow-up that adds explicit conditional exports plus a small publish script to only include needed artifacts per tag (we can use `files` in package.json to exclude dev-only bundles).

maria: also add a test matrix in CI: run samples in (node:cjs, node:esm, cloudflare) on PRs touching package.json/exports. That would have caught this.

priya: I'll open a revert PR now to unblock onboarding. Then I'll draft a new exports PR with conditional fields, typings pointer, and an update to the samples to prefer implicit imports but fallback docs for `sdk/node` & `sdk/edge`.

jamal: if you want I can help with the CI matrix change and a small script to verify `require()` vs `import` bundles at publish time.

priya: yes please. assigning follow-ups:
- priya: revert exports change (PR in 10m)
- maria: add CI matrix + tests
- jamal: helper script for publish verification
- alex: quick docs blurb for sample imports

sam: thanks, team. let's try to avoid another surprise where auth retries differ between node/edge shipments — maybe add an integration smoke that calls auth+retry paths after install.

maria: noted. also adding an issue to track typings edgecases: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1245

priya: thanks all. will paste PR numbers here when ready :thumbsup:
